doc.title: Michi Fuji interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: Goals, teaching and Nigel Kennedy
summary: Her goals are small ones, such as learning tunes; improving as a player matters more than a professorship; she likes Nigel Kennedy.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: I asked Hide about goals. I think you heard his answer when he said there’s no goals in jazz. It’s like one day to the next. What about you? Do you have goals that you think “I’d like to be doing this in a few years?”

Not that goal, but smaller goals. For example, I really want to know a lot of tunes. Just things. But that is not for the career, just for my ability. So I want to know the tunes. And I want to hear more harmony things from the piano or bass. That goal I always have. But I don’t think about the goal of a career. More the practice way. I will learn that tune. Like that goal.
Well a lot of jazz musicians have found their way into academia, teaching in colleges and so forth. Is that a goal of yours? To be a professor?

I don’t know if I’ll have a chance. I want to do anything. But for me, if my fingers are stiff because I don’t have time to practice, this is, for me, getting really frustrating. And if I couldn’t play in a session it’s not good. It’s kind of frustrating. But if I cannot stop practicing it’s all right. But to get rid of the time is not good for me. But the point, the center is the ability going up. If I can be a professor it’s fine, but the center is not teaching.
The center is that you continue to be a good player.

No that’s a good way to put it. Because if you really get involved in teaching it might take away from your time and your effort and the whole thing. There was a brief time of fusion music in the 70’s, there were some electric violin players, the Mahavishnu Orchestra. Are you familiar with any of that music? Very electric, with the violin going through —
But I like Nigel Kennedy. He’s electric. And he’s very masterful of the classic music. But I like his treatment.
